ethnicity_note: Shares of the ten ethno-linguistic categories the 2015 census sorts the country's 49 ethnic groups into, summed from the Lao Statistics Bureau's village indicator table for the census -- each village's published percentage turned back into people by its own published population, then added up over this unit. A category under 0.05% of the unit is inside the residual too. 'Other or not stated' is the census's own other-and-not-stated together with the foreign population, 1.9% of the country between them. 'Lao' here is the category and not the ethnic group: Table 1 of the Socio-Economic Atlas of the Lao PDR 2015, which defines these ten, puts the Lao of Huaphanh, Xiangkhouang, Bolikhamsai, Vientiane province and Hinboun district into 'Tai-Thay', so nationally the two come to 43.7% and 18.3% where the census's own ethnic-group table prints Lao 53.2%; together they are its Lao-Tai family, 62.4%. The census's English results volume prints this composition for the country only.
religion_note: Shares of the five religions the 2015 census counts, summed from the Lao Statistics Bureau's village indicator table for the census -- each village's published percentage turned back into people by its own published population, then added up over this unit. A category under 0.05% of the unit is inside the residual too. 'No religion or not stated' is everything the five leave, and it is large because the census defines a religion as a spiritual system with written doctrines: the animist beliefs of most non-Lao-Tai people are recorded in it, along with 1.8% of the country who stated nothing. Nationally it is 33.3%, of which the census publishes 31.4% as no religion. The census's English results volume prints this composition for the country only.
